records.title: Flying and Diving — A Unique Health Concern
records.locator: Printed p. 2 (PDF p. 2), 1961 crew account and May 1961 bulletin citation

observations.protocol: A pressurized commercial flight after same-day diving no deeper than 30 ft. Blumkin gives a cabin-altitude range from 8,000 to 10,000 ft. Flight and dive timing details are incomplete.
observations.note: The pilot was incapacitated in flight, less than 4 hours after completing the last dive.
observations.locator: Printed p. 2 (PDF p. 2), 1961 crew account and May 1961 bulletin citation

records.title: Aviation Safety Digest 43. SCUBA diving and flight.
records.locator: Issue 43, September 1965, discussion of SCUBA diving and the United States crew
records.note: The bulletin gives a United States pressurized aircraft, a day of shallow dives, an approximately 8,000-ft cabin altitude and the FAA source. The abbreviated account has no role-specific data and is likely another description of the same flight.

observations.protocol: A military aircraft lost cabin pressure after a window failed. The source describes a subsequent descent to 12,000 ft. The altitude at symptom onset and exact delay after the pressure loss remain unspecified.
observations.note: The radar navigator had knee bends during unpressurized flight. The source gives no diagnostic adjudication, recovery time or clinical follow-up.
observations.outcome_window: The symptom course in the safety narrative. Uniform clinical follow-up is unavailable.
